title: Whether each approval decision reaches exactly the tool call it was issued for, when a step's tool call ids repeat
pins: The pairing of a person's approval decision with the one tool call it was issued for. A decision reaches a call through the tool call id its approval request names, and a provider can return two calls in one step under the same id, or under an empty id. Drift here does not error: a step that paired decisions by id could run a call nobody approved, or run one call twice on one approval. When a step's tool call ids repeat (empty ids count) no gated call in that step may run, whatever was decided, every decision recorded for it is a denial, results are matched to calls by position and never by id, and no later decision or resume may revive one; a step whose ids are distinct is decided call by call. In every language.
scope: One model step with two or three calls to a gated tool `echo`, with distinct ids, one shared id, empty ids, or a shared id on two of three calls; an ungated tool `free` sharing the gated calls' id, and (0.2.0) one gated and one ungated call sharing an id or an empty id, in either order; decisions in every order, all at once or one round at a time. Each language's runtime is driven at its public seam, offline with a fake model: PHP through Prism's OpenAI Responses handler over faked HTTP with Session::decide(), TypeScript with recordDecisions(), Python with record_approval() once per decision, since it has no batch call. Rows apr-0016 to apr-0020 (0.2.0, DECISION B) supersede the parked step with a later assistant step with tool calls, an assistant text row or a user row recorded by a host (apr-0020: under the step's own run id, which a caller cannot make inside), or a new message, and record each call's outcome. Rows apr-0021 and apr-0022 (0.2.0, SEGMENT OWNERSHIP) record a later step whose call shares the parked call's id and tool, then one result row in the later step's segment carrying the EARLIER call's arguments (apr-0021: no decision, the later approval then approved; apr-0022: with the later approval, as a run writes it once its call ran, then three resumes), and record each step's outcomes read by segment. Each row also records (0.2.0) the decision the thread stored for each approval, so a language that ran nothing but kept a person's approval standing for a call that never ran disagrees. Not in these rows: approval requests that repeat a tool_call_id while the calls do not (that shape only arises from a stored row another writer produced, so it is pinned by each language's own tests), streamed decisions, plan-held and subagent steps, and the denial reason text, which each language's own tests pin. And (0.3.0, G-404) apr-0023, supersede `new_message_failed`: a new message whose own turn then fails (the provider request throws). The message and the replaced denials are recorded in ONE write before the turn is sent, so the step stays superseded and a later decision is refused `approval_not_pending`.
findings: All eleven rows agree in all three languages, and that agreement is a statement about the rule each runner was written against, not proof the rule is right. Every expectation was written before any language ran and committed before any result was recorded. The rows were probed against each harness at the commit before its G-392 change: rows apr-0004, apr-0006, apr-0007 and apr-0008 fail in all three languages there, and the distinct-id controls apr-0001 to apr-0003 pass, so the suite separates the rule from a runtime that pairs decisions by id. Rows apr-0005, apr-0009, apr-0010 and apr-0011 also passed before the change, so they pin the outcome without discriminating it. No row needed a language-specific skip: every language accepted an empty tool call id from its fake client. 0.2.0 (G-387 round 13) adds the `decided` column, the decision the thread recorded for each approval, and rows apr-0012 to apr-0015, a gated and an ungated call sharing an id or an empty id in either order. The expectations were written from the rule before any language ran. The rows the eleven had in common were silent on it: a language could run nothing and still keep a person's approval standing as approved for a call that never ran, which the Python review found. On the reference before its round-13 change, apr-0012 to apr-0015 did not park at all, because the ungated call's result was read as the gated call's, so no decision could be recorded. Until each port records its outcome no row is marked agreeing. 0.2.0 (G-387 round 13b) adds apr-0021 and apr-0022 for SEGMENT OWNERSHIP: a result counts only for the step whose segment it sits in, matched there by exact arguments, then id and tool name, then id; every outcome column is now read by segment. No earlier row's expected value depended on reading a result across segments, so none changed. The expectations were written from the rule before any language ran; the PHP reference already complied (its readers pair results only within the paused step's rows), and its runner reproduces both rows. apr-0023 (0.3.0, G-404) was written from the rule and is a defect the reference had: it wrote the replaced denials and the new message in two writes, so a turn that failed between them left the denials alone, the step still read as parked, and a decision was accepted for calls already denied.
